LECTURE FIVE
COMPUTER NETWORK MANAGEMENT
Student learning outcomes 
 
After going through this lecture, students will be able to:
Define Computer Network Management and explain its importance in modern enterprise and organizational environments.
Identify the key components of network management
Describe common network management protocols
Differentiate between centralized and distributed network management architectures.

INTRODUCTION TO COMPUTER NETWORK MANAGEMENT
Computer Network Management is the process of monitoring, administering, maintaining, and securing computer networks to ensure they operate efficiently, reliably, and securely.
It involves the use of specialized tools, protocols, policies, and procedures to control and manage network devices such as routers, switches, servers, firewalls, and wireless access points.
Network management typically follows the FCAPS model developed by the international organization for standardization, which includes:
F – fault management: detecting, isolating, and correcting network problems.
C – configuration management: managing device settings and network changes.
A – accounting management: tracking resource usage.
P – performance management: monitoring speed, traffic, and efficiency.
S – security management: protecting the network from threats and unauthorized access.

IMPORTANCE OF NETWORK MANAGEMENT IN MODERN ENTERPRISES AND ORGANIZATIONS
In today’s digital-driven world, organizations depend heavily on their networks for communication, data sharing, cloud services, and business operations. Effective network management is therefore critical for the following reasons:
1. Ensures network reliability and availability - Businesses rely on continuous connectivity for emails, cloud systems, ERP platforms, and video conferencing. Proper network management minimizes downtime and ensures high availability.
2. Improves performance and efficiency - By monitoring bandwidth usage, latency, and traffic patterns, organizations can optimize performance and prevent congestion.
3. Reduces operational costs - Proactive monitoring helps detect issues before they escalate, reducing repair costs and productivity losses caused by outages.

IMPORTANCE OF NETWORK MANAGEMENT IN MODERN ENTERPRISES AND ORGANIZATIONS
4. Enhances security - Modern enterprises face cyber threats such as malware, ransomware, and data breaches. Network management helps implement:
Access control policies
Firewall rules
Intrusion detection and prevention systems
Continuous monitoring of suspicious activities
5. Supports business continuity -Through configuration backups, disaster recovery plans, and redundancy planning, organizations can maintain operations even during failures.
6. Enables scalability - As organizations grow, network management allows seamless integration of new devices, branches, cloud services, and remote users.

IMPORTANCE OF NETWORK MANAGEMENT IN MODERN ENTERPRISES AND ORGANIZATIONS
7. Provides visibility and control
Administrators gain real-time insight into:
Network health
Device status
Traffic flows
Security events
This visibility enables informed decision-making.
Computer network management is essential for ensuring that enterprise networks remain secure, efficient, scalable, and reliable. In modern organizational environments—where digital infrastructure supports almost every business function—effective network management is not optional; it is a strategic necessity.

KEY COMPONENTS OF NETWORK MANAGEMENT
1. Network devices are the physical and virtual devices that form the backbone of a network. They generate, forward, secure, and manage data traffic.
A) routers
Connect different networks (e.g., LAN to WAN/internet).
Direct data packets based on IP addresses.
Often support routing protocols and traffic filtering.
B) switches
Connect devices within a local area network (LAN).
Forward data based on mac addresses.
Support vlans, port security, and traffic monitoring.

KEY COMPONENTS OF NETWORK MANAGEMENT
C) servers
Provide shared services such as:
File storage
Email
Databases
Web hosting
Examples include:
Windows server
Linux
D) firewalls
Protect networks by filtering incoming and outgoing traffic.
Enforce security policies.
Can be hardware-based or software-based.
These devices must be continuously monitored and configured to ensure performance, reliability, and security.

NETWORK MANAGEMENT SYSTEMS (NMS)
A Network Management System (NMS) is a software platform used by network administrators to monitor, manage, and control network infrastructure from a centralized location. It provides visibility into network performance, detects faults, and helps ensure smooth operation of network services.

Key functions of an NMS
An NMS performs several critical tasks:
Monitoring – tracks network devices and traffic in real time
Fault detection – identifies failures and alerts administrators
Configuration management – manages device settings remotely
Performance analysis – measures bandwidth, latency, uptime
Security monitoring – detects suspicious activities

CORE COMPONENTS OF AN NMS
1. Management server - The central system that collects and processes network data
2. Managed devices - Network elements such as: Routers, Switches, Servers, Firewalls
3. Agents - Software installed on devices to send data to the NMS
4. Management protocols - Communication standards used by NMS:
SNMP (simple network management protocol) – most common
ICMP – used for diagnostics
Netflow – traffic analysis

TYPES OF NMS - CENTRALIZED NMS
Network management systems can be classified based on architecture, deployment, and functionality. Each type is suited for different network sizes and organizational needs.
1.Centralized NMS - A centralized NMS uses a single management server to monitor and control the entire network.
Characteristics
One central control point
All devices report to a single server
Easier to manage and maintain
Advantages
Simple setup and administration
Lower cost for small networks
Unified monitoring dashboard
Disadvantages
Single point of failure
Limited scalability for large networks
Best For:
Small to medium organizations

TYPES OF NMS - DISTRIBUTED NMS
A distributed NMS uses multiple management servers located in different network segments.
Characteristics
Each server manages a portion of the network
Data may be aggregated to a central system
Advantages
High scalability
Fault tolerance (no single point of failure)
Better performance for large networks
Disadvantages
More complex to configure
Higher cost
Best For:
Large Enterprises and Telecom Networks

TYPES OF NMS – CLOUD-BASED NMS
A Cloud-Based NMS is hosted on the internet and accessed via a web interface.⚙️ 
Characteristics:
No on-premise installation required
Managed remotely via browser
Advantages
Accessible from anywhere
Easy scalability
Reduced hardware costs
Disadvantages
Depends on internet connectivity
Potential security concerns
Best For:
Remote organizations
Businesses with multiple branches

TYPES OF NMS – ON-PREMISES NMS
Installed and operated within an organization’s local infrastructure. Characteristics:
Full control over system and data
Hosted on local servers
Advantages
Higher data security
Customization flexibility
Disadvantages
Expensive setup and maintenance
Requires IT expertise
Best For:
Remote organizations
Businesses with multiple branches

FEATURES OF A GOOD NMS
Real-time monitoring dashboards
Automated alerts and notifications
Network mapping and visualization
Reporting and analytics
Remote configuration capabilities
Scalability for large networks
BENEFITS OF USING AN NMS
Early detection of network problems
Reduced downtime
Improved network performance
Enhanced security monitoring
Simplified network administration

NETWORK MANAGEMENT TOOLS
Network Management Tools are software applications used to monitor, analyze, configure, and secure computer networks. They are essential components of a Network Management System (NMS) and help administrators maintain efficient network operations.

Purpose of Network Management Tools
Monitor network performance in real time
Detect and troubleshoot faults
Configure and manage network devices
Enhance network security
Analyze traffic and usage patterns

CATEGORIES OF NETWORK MANAGEMENT TOOLS
Monitoring Tools
Used to observe network performance, uptime, and device health.
Examples:
Nagios - It focuses on monitoring system health and alerting administrators when issues occur.
Zabbix - Zabbix is a modern, all-in-one monitoring solution designed for real-time monitoring, visualization, and automation.
PRTG Network Monitor - It is designed to monitor network performance, devices, traffic, and applications in real time using a centralized system.
Functions:
Device status monitoring
Alert generation
Performance tracking

CATEGORIES OF NETWORK MANAGEMENT TOOLS CON’T
Packet Analysis Tools
Used to capture and inspect network packets for troubleshooting and security.
Examples:
Wireshark - Widely used network protocol analyzer (packet sniffer) that allows you to capture and examine network traffic in real time. It is essential for network troubleshooting, analysis, and security investigations.
Tcpdump - Is a powerful command-line network packet analyzer used to capture and analyze network traffic in real time. It is widely used by network administrators for troubleshooting, debugging, and security monitoring, especially on linux and unix systems.
Functions:
Deep packet inspection
Protocol analysis
Identifying network anomalies

CATEGORIES OF NETWORK MANAGEMENT TOOLS CON’T
Configuration Management Tools
Used to automate and manage network device configurations.
Examples:
Ansible - Ansible is an agentless automation tool that uses simple, human-readable scripts to automate IT tasks such as configuration, deployment, and orchestration.
Puppet - Puppet is a model-driven configuration management tool that uses agents installed on devices to maintain system configurations automatically.
Functions:
Automated configuration updates
Backup and restore configurations
Policy enforcement

CATEGORIES OF NETWORK MANAGEMENT TOOLS CON’T
Performance Management Tools
Focused on analyzing bandwidth, latency, and throughput.
Examples:
SolarWinds Network Performance Monitor - Is an enterprise-grade network monitoring and management tool developed by solarwinds. It is designed to provide real-time visibility into network performance, availability, and health.
ManageEngine OpManager - Is a comprehensive network monitoring and management tool developed by manageengine. It is designed to provide real-time monitoring, fault management, and performance analysis for network infrastructure
Functions:
Bandwidth Monitoring
Traffic Analysis
Capacity Planning

CATEGORIES OF NETWORK MANAGEMENT TOOLS CON’T
Security Management Tools
Protect networks from threats and unauthorized access.
Examples:
Snort - is an intrusion detection system (IDS) and intrusion prevention system (IPS) used to monitor network traffic and detect malicious activity in real time.
Splunk - Is a powerful security information and event management (SIEM) platform used to collect, analyze, and visualize machine data from across an organization.
Functions:
Intrusion detection and prevention
Log monitoring
Threat analysis

CATEGORIES OF NETWORK MANAGEMENT TOOLS CON’T
Traffic Analysis Tools
Analyze network traffic patterns and flow behavior.
Examples:
NetFlow Analyzer - Is a flow-based monitoring tool that analyzes network traffic using technologies like netflow, sflow, IPFIX, and j-flow.
Ntopng - is an open-source traffic monitoring and analysis tool that provides real-time visibility into network usage via a web interface.
Functions:
Traffic visualization
Bandwidth usage tracking
Detecting unusual traffic

KEY FEATURES OF NETWORK MANAGEMENT TOOLS
Real-time monitoring
Automated alerts and notifications
Reporting and analytics
Remote access and control
Scalability
